portability-baseline: DELIBERATE GNU-FIRST ordering — `stat -c %Y` must come before BSD `stat -f %m` (agent-infra#1702). MEASURED mechanism, corrected: on GNU coreutils `stat -f %m f` prints the FILESYSTEM LISTING to stdout and exits **1**, not 0 — so a BSD-first `||` arm DOES run, and the output is APPENDED (listing + epoch), which the `case ''|*[!0-9]*` guard then rejects. The disposition is unchanged (GNU-first), and the guard is what saves it. The BSD arm is not on the next line: it sits below inside the `if [ -z "$age" ]` guard (`:212`).

portability-baseline: 5 live sites, and they are NOT all one shape. FOUR are GNU-first arms of documented ladders whose BSD `stat -f` arm is in the same guarded ladder below — immediately for %Z, behind a `case`/`if` guard a few lines down for %W and %Y (`:1033` %W birth, `:1035` and `:2400` %Z ctime, `:2730` %Y mtime). The FIFTH (`:1704`) is a procfs-only %Y read guarded by `[ -r "$REAP_WT_PROC_ROOT/$pid" ]` whose fallback is `ps -o etimes=`, NOT a BSD `stat` arm — do not read it as a ladder. Line numbers are against the tree this baseline lands on; they move with unrelated edits, so re-anchor by the `stat -c` form rather than the number. `box_mtime` is a valid repair for %Y (`:1704`, `:2730`) only; birth (%W) and ctime (%Z) have no shim. This count was 2 before the +3 that landed 2026-11-01 (`e83d41a1`) and were never baselined.
